ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=kx+b$ intersects the coordinate axes at points $A(2, 0)$ and $B(0, -3)$, respectively. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx+b+3>0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since the line $y=kx+b$ intersects the axes at two points, $A(2,0)$ and $B(0,-3)$, we have:
\[
\begin{cases}
2k + b = 0 \\
b = -3
\end{cases}
\]
Thus,
\[
\begin{cases}
k=\frac{3}{2} \\
b=-3
\end{cases}
\]
Therefore, $\frac{3}{2}x+(-3)+3=\frac{3}{2}x>0$,\\
Implying $x>0$.\\
Hence, the answer is $\boxed{x>0}$.
